input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: Explore: clone families (duplicate-code consolidator) for dupehound
errors: First clippy run failed on manual_is_multiple_of (rustc 1.97 lint); used a bitmask so older CI toolchains still compile.
web/dupehound.test.mjs CLI-vs-wasm equality broke because src/lib.rs grew past the CLI's 1,000-line default skip; test now passes --max-lines 100000 to the CLI.

Portfolio Pages CI failed faq-visible.test.mjs: the page's FAQPage JSON-LD kept the old 'renamed copies' answer after the visible FAQ changed. Regenerated the JSON-LD from the visible questions; a local run of the platform/pages suite was not part of run_workflow_locally --for-changes (portfolio-pages jobs were not run), so CI caught it.

doc_friction.issue: Lists yamllint as an unmeasured Rust-port candidate, but ryl and yamllint-rs (Rust ports of yamllint) already exist on crates.io; one web search ruled it out. Updated the opinion in this PR.
--for-changes does not run dupehound-ci.yml (not on the verification-only list) and naming it asks for --force; ran its five steps by hand instead.

--for-changes skipped portfolio-pages.yml's test job, which is the one that checks FAQ JSON-LD against visible text for any venture page edit; a venture index.html edit should pull in platform/pages faq-visible.test.mjs.

notes: Idea: 'duplicate-code consolidator' from the dev-tools-in-Rust opinion. dupehound --families groups pairwise clones into families (union-find, >=50% same-file overlap), with identical counts, template hint, common dir and a removable-lines range; CLI, JSON, wasm and page table. On 11,023 .mjs files: 39,263 pairs -> 3,214 families, 1.1-1.3 s and ~575 MB with or without the flag. Top families are deliberate vendoring guarded by platform/proposal/sync.test.mjs and platform/ci/usage_contract.mjs; next step is a --guarded list. Local verification: cargo fmt/clippy/test (21 pass), wasm rebuild byte-identical, node --test 17 pass, Playwright page check, run_workflow_locally --for-changes (ventures-tests 5/5; deploy and cross-review jobs not run). No agent doc in docs/reports: README/BENCHMARK carry what the next run needs.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: Senior Rust engineer: design and implement clone-family grouping with tests, wasm/page wiring, benchmark and post, about a day and a half

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
